'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Darfur]]
**[[2021 Darfur clashes]]
***The death toll from tribal clashes, which started two days ago between [[Masalit people|Masalits]] and [[Sudanese Arabs|Arabs]] in [[Geneina]], [[West Darfur]], [[Sudan]], increases to 87 people killed and 191 more wounded. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/7/death-toll-in-darfur-tribal-violence-rises-to-87 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Afar–Somali clashes]]
**About 25 to 100 people have been killed in ongoing clashes between the [[Afar Region|Afar]] and [[Somali Region]]s of [[Ethiopia]]. Fighting had begun on Friday when the Somali Region's [[special forces]] attacked the areas of Haruk and [[Gewane]] using heavy weapons including [[machine gun]]s and [[rocket-propelled grenade]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-security/at-least-100-killed-in-border-clashes-between-ethiopias-somali-and-afar-regions-official-idUSKBN2BT2BZ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**[[Tatmadaw|Security forces]] open fire on anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] protesters, killing 15 people and wounding dozens more. A [[China|Chinese]]-owned garment factory in [[Yangon]] is also [[Arson|set on fire]] by a mob. The [[Assistance Association for Political Prisoners]] says that the junta appears to be shifting its focus from the cities to rural areas, and is "losing control" of the country. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics-idUSKBN2BU0F3 (Reuters)]
*[[Syrian civil war]]
**[[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] militants raid the town of [[al-Saan]] in [[Salamiyah District]], western [[Hama Governorate|Hama]], kidnapping dozens of people, including eight [[Syrian Army|soldiers]]. Several people are later released by the [[terror group]], while one person is reportedly killed. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/islamic-state-takes-dozens-of-hostages-in-surprise-syria-desert-attack-gvlq6cnpg (''The Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[G20]] [[finance minister]]s and [[central bank]] governors agree to extend the [[debt moratorium]] period for the [[least developed countries]] until December. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/business/g20-agrees-more-help-for-poorest-covid-hit-nations-14576278 (CNA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 16 people are killed in a [[head-on collision]] between two buses near [[Caborca]] in the [[Mexican state]] of [[Sonora]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/16-killed-14-injured-in-bus-crash-involving-mine-workers-near-us-mexico-border/ar-BB1fok4W?ocid=uxbndlbing (''USA Today'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Punjab, India]]
*****[[List of chief ministers of Punjab (India)|Chief Minister]] [[Amarinder Singh]] orders the extension of the curfew from 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. [[Indian Standard Time|IST]] to the entire [[Punjab (India)|state]], as well as banning all public gatherings, due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.indiatoday.in/coronavirus-outbreak/story/punjab-corona-covid-surge-infections-night-curfew-ban-gatherings-april30-1788168-2021-04-07 (India Today)]
****[[India]] reports a record 115,736 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2021/4/7/in-pictures-india-sees-another-record-day-of-new-virus-cases (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 7,626 new confirmed cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 659,278. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/health/coronavirus/2021/04/07/covid-daily-caseload-reaches-new-high-of-7-626-with-63-more-dead (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record 20,954 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,984,348. [https://middle-east-online.com/en/covid-19-infections-reach-new-record-iran (Middle East Online)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Qatar]]
****[[Qatar]] announces a re-imposition of the strict [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] beginning April 9, which will close restaurants, cafés, cinemas, hairdressers, museums, and libraries and ban most indoor activities, in order to reduce the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-04-qatar-reimposes-lockdown-coronavirus-surge.html (MedicalXpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****[[Pakistan]] surpasses 700,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/343829-with-102-new-fatalities-coronavirus-death-toll-crosses-15000-mark-in-pakistan (Geo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]], [[Lineage B.1.1.7]]
****[[Thailand]] reports its first locally transmitted cases of the Lineage B.1.1.7 variant first detected in the [[United Kingdom]]. It found 24 cases in the [[Thong Lor]] cluster in [[Bangkok]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2096527/uk-covid-19-strain-in-thong-lor-cluster (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belgium]]
****[[Belgium]] temporarily restricts the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to people over 55 years old following a report from the [[European Medicines Agency]] that there is a "possible link" between the vaccine and very rare [[blood clot]]ting cases. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/news/belgium-all-news/163816/belgium-will-only-use-astrazeneca-for-over-55s-for-a-month-vandenbroucke-ema/ (''The Brussels Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Estonia]]
****[[Estonia]] suspends the use of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine by people under 60 years old following a report of a possible link with cases of [[blood clot]]ting. [https://news.err.ee/1608169060/estonia-suspends-use-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-for-under-60s (Eesti Rahvusringhääling)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Bavaria]] signs a "preliminary contract" to purchase 2.5 million doses of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine]], which is subject to approval from the [[European Medicines Agency]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/04/07/bavaria-has-negotiated-preliminary-contract-for-2-5-million-doses-of-russia-s-sputnik-v-va (Euronews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Castile and León]] suspends the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine]] until the [[European Medicines Agency]]'s security report is published. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-spain-vaccines/spains-castile-and-leon-region-suspends-use-of-astrazeneca-vaccine-idUSKBN2BU0ZY (Reuters)]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Ministry of Health]] restricts the use of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to people over 60 years old following a report of a "possible link" with very rare [[blood clot]]ting. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-spain-coronavirus-pandemic-coronavirus-vaccine-760e317fab776973fd926aca5daec422 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 54,740 new confirmed cases and 276 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1839201 (Arab News)]
***[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] announces that [[blood clot]]ting should be listed as a "very rare" side effect of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] vaccine. It also insists that benefits of using the vaccine continue to outweigh the risks. [https://www.dw.com/en/astrazeneca-ema-says-blood-clots-very-rare-side-effect/a-57118315 (DW)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
****[[Argentina]] reports 22,039 new cases of COVID-19, a record for the second consecutive day. The country also reports 199 deaths. These numbers bring the total number of cases to more than 2.4 million and the total number of deaths to 56,833. [https://www.minutouno.com/sociedad/coronavirus-argentina/mas-22-mil-casos-las-ultimas-24-horas-n5182582 (''Minuto Uno'')]
****[[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] announces a three-week curfew from midnight to 6:00 p.m. beginning from April 9 to April 30 amidst a record number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/argentina-announces-curfew-as-coronavirus-cases-rise-01617837613 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Brazil]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant, which was originally detected in [[South Africa]], in a person from [[Sao Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. [https://www.news24.com/amp/news24/world/news/covid-19-brazil-detects-first-case-of-south-african-variant-20210407 (News24)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
***[[Morocco]] announces a nationwide curfew during [[Ramadan]] from 8:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. to combat the spread of [[COVID-19]]. [https://northafricapost.com/48857-covid-19-morocco-announces-nationwide-night-curfew-during-ramadan.html (North Africa Post)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Ukraine–NATO relations]], [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**[[Russia]] warns that having [[Ukraine]] join [[NATO]] "would exacerbate the Donbass conflict" after Ukraine urged NATO to "speed up" its membership application. [https://meduza.io/en/feature/2021/04/07/we-deeply-doubt-it-will-help (Meduza)]
*[[Myanmar–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[Myanmar]]'s Ambassador to the [[United Kingdom]], [[Kyaw Zwar Minn]], is dismissed by a [[military attaché]] and locked out of the [[Embassy of Myanmar, London|embassy]] in [[London]]. British Foreign Secretary [[Dominic Raab]] condemns the "bullying actions" but says the UK has accepted the change. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-56670524 BBC News]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Northern Ireland riots]]
**In west [[Belfast]], [[Ulster loyalism|Loyalist]] youths [[Motor vehicle theft|hijack]] a bus and [[arson|set it on fire]]. A photographer is also assaulted and his cameras are damaged. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2021/0407/1208499-northern-ireland/ (RTÉ News)]
*[[Cannabis in Ukraine]]
**The [[Verkhovna Rada]] votes to legalize the use of [[medical cannabis]] products. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/ukraine-legalizes-certain-types-of-medical-cannabis-products.html (Kyiv Post)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of the Netherlands]]
**[[Vera Bergkamp]] of the [[Democrats 66]] party is elected as [[Speaker of the House of Representatives (Netherlands)|Speaker]] of the [[House of Representatives (Netherlands)|House of Representatives]], becoming the first [[List of LGBT firsts by year|lesbian]] legislative speaker in the [[States General of the Netherlands|Dutch legislature]]. [https://www.dutchnews.nl/news/2021/04/d66-mp-vera-bergkamp-is-the-new-parliamentary-chairwoman/ (DutchNews)]
*[[Censorship in Italy]]
**The [[government of Italy|government]] formally repeals a 1913 law, which allows the government to censor or ban films, effectively outlawing [[film censorship]] in the country. [https://variety.com/2021/film/news/italy-abolishes-film-censorship-1234945537/ (''Variety'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[FIFA]] indefinitely bans [[Chad national football team|Chad]] from all global [[association football|football]] competitions, citing [[Government of Chad|government]] interference in the country's football federation. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/africa/56661109 (BBC News)]
